{{short description|Portuguese-American mathematician}}
[[File:Irene Fonseca.jpg|thumb|220px|Irene Fonseca]]
'''Irene Maria Quintanilha Coelho da Fonseca''' is a Portuguese-American [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]], the Kavčić-Moura University Professor of Mathematics at [[Carnegie Mellon University]], where she directs the Center for [[Nonlinear analysis|Nonlinear Analysis]], which is part of the [[Mellon College of Science]]'s Department of [[Mathematical sciences|Mathematical Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.cmu.edu/mcs/news-events/2018/0220_Fonseca-Kavcic-Moura-Professorship.html|title=Irene Fonseca Named Kavčić-Moura Professor of Mathematics|date=February 20, 2018|publisher=CMU Mellon College of Science|access-date=2021-09-09|archive-date=2021-06-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210612113305/https://www.cmu.edu/mcs/news-events/2018/0220_Fonseca-Kavcic-Moura-Professorship.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.cmu.edu/math/cna/people/faculty/fonseca.html|title= Irene Fonseca|publisher=CMU Mellon College of Science|access-date=2024-01-05}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Fonseca was born in [[Portugal]], and did her undergraduate studies at the [[University of Lisbon]].<ref name="newsmaker">{{citation|title=Newsmaker: Irene Fonseca|newspaper=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review|first=Mike|last=Wereschagin|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-30224245.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150329111750/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-30224245.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=March 29, 2015|via=[[HighBeam Research]]|url-access=subscription |date=December 1, 2011}}.</ref> She earned a Ph.D. from the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1985, under the supervision of [[David Kinderlehrer]], who later followed his student to CMU.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=5604|name=Irene Maria Quintanilha Coelho da Fonseca}}</ref> She joined the CMU faculty after postdoctoral studies in [[Paris, France]].<ref name="newsmaker"/>

In 2011, Fonseca was elected president of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]],<ref name="newsmaker"/> serving in office from 2013 to 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leadership |url=https://www.siam.org/about-siam/leadership#Presidents |access-date=2024-01-05 |website=SIAM |language=en-US}}</ref> She also served on the Mathematical Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] in 2014 and 2015. Furthermore, she is currently serving as the Chair of [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]'s Activity Group on Mathematical Aspects of Materials Science, with the term lasting until December 31, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SIAM Activity Group on Mathematical Aspects of Materials Science|url=https://www.siam.org/membership/activity-groups/detail/mathematical-aspects-of-materials-science |access-date=2024-01-05 |website=SIAM |language=en-US}}</ref>

In addition, Fonseca was elected to serve as a Vice President of the [[American Mathematical Society]] for a three-year term, beginning in February 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=American Mathematical Society Election Results Science|url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/elections/election-results |access-date=2024-01-05 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Books==
Fonseca is the co-author of:
*''Degree Theory in Analysis and Applications'' (with Wilfrid Gangbo, [[Oxford University Press]], 1995)<ref>Review of ''Degree Theory in Analysis and Applications'': J. V. A. Gonçalves (1996), {{MR|1373430}}</ref>
*''Modern Methods in the Calculus of Variations: L<sup>P</sup> Spaces'' (with Giovanni Leoni, [[Springer Verlag]], 2007)<ref>Review of ''Modern Methods in the Calculus of Variations'': Erik J. Balder (2008), {{MR|2341508}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Fonseca is a knight of the [[Order of Saint James of the Sword]].<ref name="newsmaker"/>
She was awarded the [[AWM-SIAM Sonia Kovalevsky Lecture|Kovalevsky Award and Lecture]] in 2006<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kovalevsky Lectures |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/kovalevsky-lectures/ |access-date=2026-04-11 |website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) |language=en-US}}</ref>, and in 2009, Fonseca was elected as a fellow of SIAM "for contributions to nonlinear partial differential equations and the calculus of variations".<ref>[http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2009#Irene_Fonseca SIAM Fellows list], retrieved 2013-01-21.</ref> In 2012 she became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-21.</ref> She is also a former AMS Council member at large.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en |archive-date=2023-03-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306081906/https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2021, she was elected to the European Academy of Sciences (EURASC)<ref>{{Cite web |title= Members - European Academy of Sciences|url=https://www.eurasc.eu/members/fonsecaandrew-cmu-edu/member/ |access-date=2024-01-05 |website=European Academy of Sciences |date=13 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref> and, in 2022, she received the Senior Prize from the [[International Society for the Interaction of Mechanics and Mathematics]] for "her outstanding contributions to the calculus of variations and the mathematics of materials science, along with her exemplary service to the mathematical community and for being an inspirational mentor and role model for female mathematicians."<ref>{{Cite web |title= ISIMM award|url=https://isimm.net/ISIMM-award/ |access-date=2024-01-05 |website=International Society for the Interaction of Mechanics and Mathematics |language=en}}</ref>
